# PIXL

PIXL is a pixel-art production agent profile and skill system for Claude and Codex. This repository develops that profile, its operational skills, and the tools and knowledge that support its work. The intended outcome is coherent UI and game assets produced through the official PixelLab platform from project-specific references, inspected, integrated, and preserved with enough context for another agent or session to continue.

**Overall request remains open.** The [overall plan and TODO](TODO.md) is the current development work list: ordered remaining outcomes, evidence, completion criteria and next action. Completed increments below do not mean the specialist ecosystem is finished.

**Current stage: scoped production demonstrated; broader reliability remains in development.** Allocation, first-request preparation, connected authoring, durable provider recovery, inspection and family delivery are implemented. [Official PixelLab production](evidence/pixellab-family-production/README.md) records actual generated assets and repairs; [successor acceptance](evidence/successor-acceptance/README.md) records motion/family review in both existing consumers. [Named Codex qualification](evidence/named-codex-role/README.md) passes one explicitly registered role and same-child recovery/handoff. The [artistic-revision task](evidence/artistic-revision/README.md) uses a named Codex successor to complete the retained Claude-authored corrected29 proposal with fresh acceptance of existing artwork; all task-outcome checks pass, while an outer recorder failure keeps the overall trial partial. These scoped results retain caller corrections and failed evidence. [Useful native production](evidence/native-production/README.md) now reaches actual caller consumption in both hosts: Codex passes 35/35 checks and Claude 40/40 after two guided same-parent/same-child recoveries, including a family-directory runtime correction. Exact tested kits and original failures remain retained. Automatic discovery, broader host reliability, independent artistic consistency and other asset/engine classes remain open. The [last complete verifier](evidence/test-results.json) establishes its recorded implementation checks, not general production readiness. [PLAN](PLAN.md), [SHELVED](SHELVED.md) and [TODO](TODO.md) carry the remaining work.

**Consumer setup:** the read-only readiness report distinguishes installed files, supplied host observations and provider visibility. [Fresh installation and native results](evidence/readiness/README.md) qualify copied-kit, wheel and locked source local use, Codex's explicit portable role, and Claude's authenticated plugin route, including omitted-role/plugin cases in both hosts. Earlier authentication blocks and grader corrections remain preserved; these scoped local outcomes do not establish provider access or broader reliability. Follow the [consumer-first setup guide](docs/AGENT-KIT.md#set-up-a-consumer-project) and [declared install/update support matrix](docs/INSTALL-SUPPORT.md) for qualified runtime routes, relocation and cold recovery limits.

**Caller handoff:** the opt-in [compact caller result](evidence/caller-result/README.md) keeps full observations and exact continuation behind verified locators, with structured local recovery. Codex completes the scoped operation at 28/28 independent checks. The original Claude attempt retains its incomplete HTTP-429/timeout result. A later guided continuation completes the same retained caller assignment at 31/31 checks plus a separate 22/22 review; its frozen-kit scope and broader reliability limits remain explicit.

**Candidate/family review:** [review-context and candidate-review](spec/candidate-review.md) expose literal criteria and exact bindings, retain explicit observations, and connect nomination/completion with recoverable retries. The specialist still supplies actual visual and destination judgments. Prepared inspection packets retain their existing view-coverage rules.

**Consumer deliverable index:** `family STATE OUTPUT --view consumer --root ROOT`
(`pixl_family` with `view: "consumer"` and `output`) returns the current nominated
package's named files, exact supporting sources, declared integration choices,
current review and unresolved conditions. An explicit `--candidate` inspects a
retained historical package; it never silently selects the newest snapshot.
Export the full JSON and transfer its named files and required source modules for
cold integration. The [index contract](spec/deliverable-index.md) separates
immutable creation status from current review and keeps missing layout facts
unresolved. [NF-07's final-source cold caller](evidence/deliverable-index/README.md)
passes 43/43 independent checks with actual 1×/3× playback. Earlier source-drift
and lint failures remain retained; artistic and human acceptance stay separate.

**Isolated consumer execution:** [`consumer-execute`](spec/consumer-execution.md) runs the shipped queue-motion profile, checks actual frame/wrap and reduced-motion-switch observations, and retains exact delivered-file evidence. It leaves production state and acceptance unchanged. [TM-07 results and limits](evidence/consumer-execution/README.md) track the scoped qualification; M1/M2 and broader M3 remain open.

**Historical HTTP integration milestone complete for the controlled test.** Claude and Codex each delegated to PIXL, submitted through the official HTTP adapter, retrieved and inspected the fixture, and saved an independent parent review. See the [recorded outcomes](evidence/delegated-asset-request/README.md) and [milestone contract](evaluations/delegated-asset-request.spec.md). Provider transport was simulated; these results establish the delivery workflow, not newly generated artwork or target-engine quality.

**Project asset requirements:** use `$plar` in Codex or `/plar` in Claude to create or update the consumer project's `plar.txt`, then hand a selected asset to PIXL for paid official PixelLab production. The selected-asset path now uses `pixl_plar_prepare` / `plar prepare` to turn reviewed arguments and candidate criteria into the durable first request; [workflow and actual results](evidence/plar-allocation/README.md). Read the [critical review and A–E answers](docs/PLAR-REVIEW.md), [PLAR skill](plugins/pixl/skills/plar/SKILL.md) and [worked consumer project](examples/plar-project/README.md).

**Request and criteria handoff:** the specialist returns the exact proposed request, reference inputs and acceptance criteria; the calling agent compares them with the original sources and retains its own review before adoption. [Earlier native results](evidence/request-review/README.md) retain controlled delivery and original failures. [Targeted handoff repairs](evidence/handoff-repair/README.md), [criteria comparison](evidence/criteria-handoff/README.md) and [focused successor authoring](evidence/focused-authoring/README.md) record later corrections and remaining interrupted/native-route gaps. [The operation](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/request-review.md) keeps contract agreement, delivered-file review and actual provider quality distinct.

**Delegate visual work:** give PIXL the consumer root, a selected asset or direct brief, reference roles, and the existing decisions and authorization. The specialist chooses the PixelLab operation and returns files, findings and resumable context. Start with the [agent-to-agent contract](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/delegation.md), [official-operation guide](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/pixellab-operations.md), [connection templates](docs/AGENT-KIT.md#connect-official-pixellab), and [reference-aware example](examples/delegation/README.md). The [development review](docs/AGENT-HANDOFF-REVIEW.md) answers the required A–E questions.

For repository development, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Reading or editing PIXL's profile does not activate it. Invoke the production profile when the task is to perform pixel-art work.

The UDL is designed for agent operation. Human readability is not a wire-design criterion. Host Markdown, JSON and TOML exist at the Claude/Codex/MCP boundary; the operational project language is `.px`.

## Use it

Find the latest applicable implementation, native and actual-output receipts in the
[task-based evidence index](evidence/README.md), with direct failure and scope links.

Use the [capability/outcome matrix](docs/CAPABILITY-OUTCOMES.md) to choose a useful route, see what actually worked in each host and consumer, and identify the next unqualified condition. Human acceptance is recorded separately from development qualification.

For an asset assignment, start with the [everyday production guide](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/everyday.md):
select the actual queue/asset, prepare or resume the official request, review the
candidate and family, and return usable files with a saved continuation.

1. Load the complete PIXL kit in the consumer project through the [host setup](docs/AGENT-KIT.md#set-up-a-consumer-project).
   The profile and skills make PIXL the visual specialist; a Python installation
   alone does not register the host's agent or skills.
2. Keep the host's official PixelLab connection available for production. The
   local CLI/MCP supports requirements, state, inspection and handoff; it does not
   replace the official provider. Inspect the actual connected tool declarations.
3. Give PIXL the consumer root, selected asset or brief, reference roles and
   existing choices/authorization. The caller receives actual files, findings
   and a precise continuation.

The complete portable kit is [`plugins/pixl`](plugins/pixl). Its consumer runtime
needs Python 3.11+, Pillow and jsonschema, without maintainer tooling. Follow the
[copied-kit instructions](docs/AGENT-KIT.md#set-up-a-consumer-project) for a selected
environment and host entrypoint. A wheel is an alternative local-runtime
distribution; it does not install skills or register a named specialist.

When setup is uncertain, use the [read-only readiness report](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/readiness.md):

```text
python ABSOLUTE_KIT/scripts/pixl.py readiness --root CONSUMER --host codex --installation ABSOLUTE_KIT
```

Use the selected interpreter and quote paths containing spaces. The report
separates installed files, caller-supplied host observations and tool visibility;
it performs no authentication or generation probe. The [hash and path reference](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/identities-and-paths.md)
explains the distinct installation, consumer and store roots during production.

## Maintain this repository

The project is uv managed. Keep the existing `.venv`; the current development environment uses Python 3.14.3 (the package declares Python 3.11 or newer):

```powershell
uv sync --locked
uv build
uv run --no-sync python scripts/verify.py
uv run --no-sync python -m pixl sources --root .
uv run --no-sync python -m pixl workflow examples/intake/project.px --root .
uv run --no-sync python -m pixl validate examples/atelier/project.px --root .
uv run --no-sync python -m pixl context examples/atelier/project.px produce
```

The default development sync keeps lint, type-checking, build and benchmark tools
in the dev group. `uv sync --locked --no-dev` is a runtime-only source-checkout
route; it needs this repository and lockfile. It is not required for a consumer
using a complete copied kit. Tokenizer benchmarking remains in the optional
`benchmark` extra as well as the maintainer environment.

For a read-only check of current package inputs and retained capability claims, run
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -B scripts/check_integrity.py`. The
[integrity guide](docs/EVIDENCE-INTEGRITY.md) explains historical results, stale
current applicability and exact recovery actions. The command prints a report
without rebuilding packages or evidence.

The verifier archives previous generated evidence, regenerates local fixtures and the plugin, discovers the entire test suite, and builds/installs a wheel through its source distribution. Each attempt has its own directory under `evidence/verification-runs/`; a failed stage leaves a current failure report and identifies unperformed stages. See [verification scope](docs/VERIFICATION.md) for separate lint/type checks and evidence limits.

The checked-in source adapters expose `$pixl` in Codex and `/pixl` in Claude;
Claude also supports `claude --agent pixl` from this checkout. Consumer/plugin
entrypoints have their own paths and names in [AGENT-KIT.md](docs/AGENT-KIT.md).
No global configuration is changed by the kit.

## Scaffold mechanisms

- **PIXL/1:** 13 typed record kinds for actors, projects, sources, runtime dependencies, visual contracts, knowledge, decisions, tasks, assets, evidence, remote jobs and handoff context. Deterministic grammar, canonical hashes, closed schemas, dependency ordering and complete context selection.
- **PIXL/2 lifecycle:** explicit choices, planned outputs, criteria and immutable verdicts. Start with `intake`, save the acceptance plan before evaluation, and use `workflow` to distinguish unperformed, failed, unavailable and passing checks. A sample can investigate a proposal; production adoption has stronger gates. The [operational skill](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/intake-sample.md) covers the complete local sequence.
- **Family delivery:** exact approved sample dependencies, ordered member plans, collective continuity and destination criteria, immutable copied files and historical snapshot drift. The [family skill](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/family-delivery.md) connects actual comparison and revision to `family` / `family-snapshot`; retaining a package creates no acceptance.
- **Candidate inspection:** exact native/nearest views, explicit frame/tile context, source-bound measurements and retained reviewer declarations. The [inspection skill](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/inspection.md) uses `inspection-prepare`, host viewing and `inspection-review`; `inspection` recovers original conditions, failures and viewing limits. The runtime supplies no automatic artistic verdict.
- **State runtime:** revision-checked commits, local writer exclusion, immutable snapshots, immutable proof receipts with explicit supersession, source/artifact drift checks and mandatory reopening of affected completed tasks.
- **Pixel-art knowledge:** 43 curated methods with 93 reviewed current source locators and 39 freshly executed reference checks. The compiled [PIXL library](knowledge/library.px) contains prerequisites, procedures, checks, pitfalls, sources and bound proof receipts. The [knowledge operation](plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/knowledge.md) takes a production question through source discovery, exact retrieval, applicability assessment and a specific next proof. [Coverage](methods/method-proof-coverage.json) states each reference proof's limits.
- **PixelLab preparation:** a historical snapshot of 100 documented MCP tools and 454 parameters, dated official documentation, exact caller-supplied schema validation, cross-field rules, deterministic intent identity and observation-based job journaling.
- **Optional PixelLab HTTP adapter:** one official async image endpoint, exact retained OpenAPI schema, durable submission/polling and PNG import. A separate opt-in MCP bridge exposes it; tests replace its HTTP transport and block sockets.
- **Agent kit:** one shared PIXL expert profile, Claude/Codex adapters, a portable runtime, and the [declared local MCP tools](pixl/mcp.py). The actual authenticated PixelLab connection remains with the host harness.

# Find evidence from the public entrypoint

1. **authority** — Can the corrected 20-to-29 requirement successor (CF-03) be described as an overall passing trial? Locate its task outcome, governing overall result and remaining failure.

2. **art** — Find the actual animation-art revision outcome and the terrain/animation diagnostic qualification. Which evidence supports actual art revision, native production, fault diagnosis and later package consumption? Keep these scopes separate.

3. **gaps** — Does the available evidence qualify native continuation through updates or relocation, or production outcomes for normal maps/materials and rigs? Locate the authoritative limits and state what a passing local check cannot establish.

4. **applicability** — Explain how a retained passing receipt can have stale applicability, and why CURRENT-FULL-VERIFICATION can differ from the latest full checkpoint. Which registered claims presently have current evidence? Explain how to check again without rebuilding evidence.

Return NAVIGATION-RESULT.json with version:1, status:'complete' or 'incomplete',
entrypoint, a route array naming the repository-relative documents followed, and
answers (one per question). Each answer has id, conclusion, evidence (an array of
{path,sha256} references to exact local files), limits (strings), and prior_failures
(exact file references where applicable). Quote only small relevant facts; do not
copy large receipts. Cite exact receipt paths and hashes rather than relying only
on an index summary. If a fact cannot be found, state that gap; do not infer a pass.
At the end, report any confusing navigation, contradictory current-facing wording,
or missing route in navigation_observations (strings). No post-launch help will be
provided. Do not write the evaluator's grade or alter any original artifact.

# Check evidence before relying on a release

Run the maintainer integrity check when choosing which existing result supports
a current capability or package. It reads the checkout, the declared bundle and
the retained evidence registry. It prints what is intact, what changed and the
next useful action. It creates no files, rebuilds nothing and invokes no tests,
native hosts, browsers or provider operations.

```powershell
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -B scripts/check_integrity.py
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -B scripts/check_integrity.py --json
```

Use `--claim ID` to inspect a named claim from the report; repeat it for several
claims. Package checks still run. `--root PATH` selects another checkout, and
`--manifest PATH` selects a registry relative to that root. The command remains
an inspection operation in every mode. Save stdout separately when retaining a
new audit; keep earlier results and use a fresh destination.

## Read the result

| Result | Meaning | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intact, current bindings | Registered receipts and claim wording match; the declared tested inputs still match current files | Use the result within its recorded scope and evidence tier |
| Intact, historical | The original receipt is unchanged; its outcome belongs to the recorded source/package and assignment | Keep that result as historical evidence; qualify changed work separately |
| Stale current applicability | A source, package or inventory differs from the inputs recorded by a claim that is intended to apply now | Inspect the named paths and rerun the affected proof when current qualification is needed |
| Changed or missing evidence | A pinned receipt/artifact cannot be verified, or a recorded field differs | Recover the exact retained bytes or record the unresolved gap; preserve the original receipt |
| Changed claim wording | The anchored claim line differs from its reviewed registry binding | Review the new wording against its evidence before updating the registry |
| Invalid declaration | The registry, pointer, path or package structure is malformed or unsupported | Correct that declaration; the check does not guess its meaning |

Exit codes are **0** for intact current/historical checks, **1** when review is
needed, and **2** for invalid input. A recorded failed trial can have intact
evidence. It remains a failed trial. Source drift identifies a qualification gap;
it does not prove a runtime regression. A passing integrity check does not run
or repeat the checks inside a receipt.

<a id="integrity-full-verification"></a>The retained SC-06 full-verification result is a historical pass. Applying it to the current checkout requires its recorded source hashes and source inventory to match; later implementation or test changes retain the original pass while making current applicability stale.

<a id="integrity-claim-review"></a>The dated NF-04 capability review remains a historical review. Its original reviewed-source identities can be checked against today's documents, but unchanged receipt bytes do not establish that later claim wording was reviewed.

The default report can therefore need review even when the current bundle still
matches its canonical sources. Keep the full-suite result and newer focused
results separate. Do not regenerate old evidence, overwrite a failed receipt or
change an expected hash simply to obtain a zero exit code.

The [TM-10 qualification](../evidence/release-integrity/README.md) exercises the

The [NF-07 update](../evidence/deliverable-index/README.md) adds two reviewed claims

## What is checked

The [claim registry](../evaluations/evidence-claims.json) connects selected
[core capability rows](CAPABILITY-OUTCOMES.md#core-tasks) and maintenance claims
to explicit retained receipts, exact outcome fields, tested sources and package
identities. Each claim names its scope, evidence tier and limitations. The
registry is reviewed metadata, not an automated interpretation of every sentence
or every advertised domain.

Receipt hashes and exact JSON-pointer assertions protect the registered
historical facts. Source/package bindings compare today's files with hashes
inside those pinned receipts. Whole-source inventory checks additionally detect
new files that an older hash map never tested. The checker follows only explicit
registered references; old Windows temporary paths and Linux `/tmp` execution
locators remain historical context.

Release checks use the same pure payload plan as the bundle builder. They
compare the expected file/source set, payload bytes, supplied-source inventory,
version and generated runtime requirements. This catches an internally
consistent but stale bundle, omitted manifest entries and new source files.
Selected retained wheel/sdist bytes are inspected in place, with no extraction,
installation or build. A package version or matching filename is never used as
a substitute for the exact archive digest.

This command is a maintainer operation. Consumers continue through
[setup and readiness](AGENT-KIT.md#set-up-a-consumer-project) and the
[declared support matrix](INSTALL-SUPPORT.md). Integrity does not establish
authentication, native instruction following, new art, visual quality or
target-engine acceptance. Human acceptance stays separate and unrecorded.

## Maintain the registry

Use a stable claim ID and a unique HTML anchor on the actual claim line. Bind
the line's UTF-8 bytes without its line ending, so unrelated documentation edits
do not invalidate that claim. An intentional wording change requires a review
of its scope before replacing that line binding.

Register exact repository-relative receipt/artifact paths and SHA-256 identities.
Select outcome/assertion fields with explicit JSON pointers. Derive current
source/package bindings from the tested hashes in those receipts; hashing today's
untested code does not create a tested-source binding. Preserve original failed
and partial outcomes alongside recovery evidence. Mark historical claims as
historical and keep their original package identity.

The version-1 registry rejects duplicate IDs/JSON keys, unknown fields, malformed
digests, unsupported versions, ambiguous bindings and paths that escape the
selected checkout. A current claim needs explicit tested-input bindings. Its
limits must continue to distinguish local mechanics, native behavior and actual
task outcomes. The checker reports its own source and registry identities so a
saved report can be tied to the exact inspection implementation.

The mutating [full verifier](VERIFICATION.md) remains a separate operation. Read
its side effects before running it. TM-10 integrity work does not close M1/M2 or
broader M3/M4/M5, and it does not require human approval to continue development.

## Planning, knowledge and reference authority

<a id="core-retain"></a>
When imported library sources change after a kit update, use [`retain-library` / `pixl_retain_library`](../plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/library-retention.md) to keep or recover the exact declared revisions from retained bytes or the original kit. The [local recovery evidence](../evidence/library-retention/README.md), [eight-operation replay](../evidence/library-retention/20261107/reproduction-after.json) and [portable recovery](../evidence/library-retention/20261107/portable-recovery.json) establish **L** resumption/relocation with unchanged state and receipts. This was not a fresh native model trial; old proof does not qualify a changed method or new art, and missing original bytes cannot be reconstructed.

<a id="core-plan"></a>
For dependent samples, family members and revisions, use [production-plan and stage-prepare](../spec/production-plan.md) to preserve reviewed dependencies and bind accepted upstream candidates to the next request. # Check evidence before relying on a release Run the maintainer integrity check when choosing which existing result supports a current capability or package. It reads the checkout, the declared bundle and the retained evidence registry. It prints what is intact, what changed and the next useful action. It creates no files, rebuilds nothing and invokes no tests, native hosts, browsers or provider operations. ```powershell .venv/Scripts/python.exe -B scripts/check_integrity.py .venv/Scripts/python.exe -B scripts/check_integrity.py --json ``` Use `--claim ID` to inspect a named claim from the report; repeat it for several claims. Package checks still run. `--root PATH` selects another checkout, and `--manifest PATH` selects a registry relative to that root. The command remains an inspection operation in every mode. Save stdout separately when retaining a new audit; keep earlier results and use a fresh destination. ## Read the result | Result | Meaning | Next action | | --- | --- | --- | | Intact, current bindings | Registered receipts and claim wording match; the declared tested inputs still match current files | Use the result within its recorded scope and evidence tier | | Intact, historical | The original receipt is unchanged; its outcome belongs to the recorded source/package and assignment | Keep that result as historical evidence; qualify changed work separately | | Stale current applicability | A source, package or inventory differs from the inputs recorded by a claim that is intended to apply now | Inspect the named paths and rerun the affected proof when current qualification is needed | | Changed or missing evidence | A pinned receipt/artifact cannot be verified, or a recorded field differs | Recover the exact retained bytes or record the unresolved gap; preserve the original receipt | | Changed claim wording | The anchored claim line differs from its reviewed registry binding | Review the new wording against its evidence before updating the registry | | Invalid declaration | The registry, pointer, path or package structure is malformed or unsupported | Correct that declaration; the check does not guess its meaning | Exit codes are **0** for intact current/historical checks, **1** when review is needed, and **2** for invalid input. A recorded failed trial can have intact evidence. It remains a failed trial. Source drift identifies a qualification gap; it does not prove a runtime regression. A passing integrity check does not run or repeat the checks inside a receipt. The retained SC-06 full-verification result is a historical pass. Applying it to the current checkout requires its recorded source hashes and source inventory to match; later implementation or test changes retain the original pass while making current applicability stale. The dated NF-04 capability review remains a historical review. Its original reviewed-source identities can be checked against today's documents, but unchanged receipt bytes do not establish that later claim wording was reviewed. The default report can therefore need review even when the current bundle still matches its canonical sources. Keep the full-suite result and newer focused results separate. Do not regenerate old evidence, overwrite a failed receipt or change an expected hash simply to obtain a zero exit code.
